subject: Re: Fee corridor reconciliation & order form amendment
messages:
From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmehealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fee corridor math + request for a single-line amendment on Exhibit C

Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is enthusiastic. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up with two discrete asks so we can get the order form across the finish line: 

1) The pricing exhibit (Exhibit C) has the quarterly fee "corridor" language that caps overage credits when usage drops below Floor X. Our finance team wants a short engineering-friendly table showing the per-unit effective rate at three bands (<=Floor, Floor+1..Cap, >Cap) so they can model run-rate impact for 2027. Can you provide that?

2) Legal noticed the current redline still includes the phrase "no retroactive true-up beyond 60 days" — they want a single-line amendment that clarifies "true-ups will apply to invoices issued within 120 days of the usage period end". They prefer minimal contract language pasted into the order form rather than another bulky amendment PDF.

I've attached the order form doc we pulled from our side (Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf) and a short suggested clause (Acme_Redline_12192026.docx) for reference. Would you and your legal/sales ops folks prefer we mark up, or do you want Redwood to propose the single-line insertion?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming for the 23rd if possible.

Best,
Jared Bloom
Head of Procurement
Acme Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee corridor math + request for a single-line amendment on Exhibit C

Jared — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick answers:

- We can produce the three-band effective-rate table by EOD Monday (21st). We'll include both per-token and per-embedding illustrative rows so your finance team can plug numbers.
- Redwood is happy to propose the single-line insertion into Exhibit C rather than iterate on your doc. Our legal prefers adding the clause directly under the "Billing & True-ups" section to keep change history clean.

Rishi (cc'd) — can your team prepare the table and proposed contract language? Laura, can you confirm this is OK from orderform/ops side for our standard processing?

Jared — can you confirm Acme prefers the clause to reference "invoices issued within 120 days of the usage period end" verbatim (we will mirror that language)? Also confirm the definition of "usage period" — calendar quarter vs. billing month? If quarter, we'll model using quarterly buckets.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee corridor math + request for a single-line amendment on Exhibit C

Soojin / Laura / Jared — attaching my draft outputs below (pasted so you have immediate visibility; attachments follow).

--- Effective-rate summary (illustrative) ---
Band A: Usage <= Floor (50k token-units / month)
- Per-token effective rate: $0.0025
- Rationale: applies minimum guarantee; no overage credits

Band B: Usage > Floor up to Cap (50k - 250k token-units / month)
- Per-token blended rate: $0.0019
- Rationale: blended between committed units and metered overage pricing; assumes 30% overage smoothing

Band C: Usage > Cap (above 250k token-units / month)
- Per-token marginal rate: $0.0014
- Rationale: tier-discounter applied for sustained high-volume usage; volume rebate triggers after Cap is exceeded for a rolling quarter

Notes: I'll export a simple 3x2 table (band x {per-token, per-embedding}) and attach as CSV. These are modeled off the order form's current tiers; if Acme's finance prefers calendar-quarter aggregation we should rerun quickly.

--- Proposed single-line insertion (to go into Exhibit C under "Billing & True-ups") ---
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Provider and Customer agree that any invoice true-up related to usage during a given usage period shall be issued within one hundred and twenty (120) days following the end of such usage period; Provider shall not assert retroactive true-ups for usage outside of such period.
"

If Acme wants slightly different verb tense or to avoid the phrase "retroactive", we can tweak. Laura — from ops perspective this is straightforward, but we should ensure our billing platform can lock the windows per the defined 120-day period. Jared, confirm the usage period (quarter vs month) and I'll attach the CSV table for the three bands.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee corridor math + request for a single-line amendment on Exhibit C

Thanks, Rishi — that table looks like exactly what finance asked for. Confirming: Acme wants "usage period" defined as calendar quarter. The procurement team also prefers avoiding the word "retroactive". Suggested minor edit below for Redwood to include in Exhibit C (we're happy with Redwood to insert):

"Any invoice true-up related to usage during a given calendar quarter shall be issued within one hundred and twenty (120) days following the end of such calendar quarter; Provider will not apply true-ups for usage that falls outside that 120-day issuance window."

If you can accept that language and attach the CSV, we'll route the updated PDF to our legal for a final run. Appreciate the quick turn.

— Jared
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmehealth.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -0800

Hi Jared — thanks for the precise edit; Redwood is OK to accept that wording with one small operational caveat: our billing system records usage windows by invoice period tied to calendar quarter but final computations run in a batch on day +7 of the following quarter. The 120-day issuance window is compatible, but we will need to preserve the billing-run audit trail for any true-up disputes. We'll add an automated note on the invoice ("billing-run date: YYYY-MM-DD") for transparency.

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v3_filled.pdf (with Exhibit C updated) and Acme_BandTable_3x2.csv. Please confirm that PDF works for Acme legal and we'll arrange signature steps (DocuSign link included below).
